source_text: Quibus duobus dominis neget posse seruiri, quia alterum offendi sit necesse alterum defendi, ipse declarat, deum proponens et mamonam. proinde mamonam quem intellegi uelit, si interpretem non habes, ab ipso potes discere. admonens enim nos de saecularibus suffragia nobis prospicere amicitiarum secundum serui illius exemplum, qui ab actu summotus dominicos debitores diminutis cautionibus releuat in subsidium sibi: et ego, inquit, dico uobis, facite uobis amicos de mamona iniustitiae, de nummo scilicet, de \' quo et seruus ille. iniustitiae enim auctorem et dominatorem totius saeculi nummum scimus omnes. cui famulatam uidens Pharisaeorum cupiditatem ammentauit hanc sententiam: non potestis deo seruire et mamonae. inridebant denique Pharisaei pecuniae cupidi, quod intellexissent scilicet mamonam de nummo dictum, ne quia existimet in mamona creatorem intellegendum et Christum a creatoris illos seruitute reuocasse.. quid nunc? potius ex hoc disce unum a Christo deum ostensum. duos enim dominos nominauit, deum et mamonam, crea. torem et nummum: denique non potestis deo seruire, utique ei, cui uidebantur seruire, et mamonam, cui magis destinabantur. quodsi ipse alium se ageret, non duos dominos, sed tres demonstrasset — et creator enim dominus, quia deus, et utique magis dominus quam mamonas magisque homini obseruandus, qua magis dominus —; quale est enim, ut qui mamonam dominum dixerat et cum domino iunxerat uero, ipsum dominum taceret, id est deum creatorem? aut numquid tacendo eo concessit seruiendum ei esse, si solummodo sibi et mamonae negauit posse seruiri? ita cum unum deum ponit, nominaturus et creatorem, si alius esset ipse, creatorem nominauit quem [dominum] sine alio [deo non] posuit. et illud itaque relucebit, quomodo dictum sit: (si) in mamona iniusto fideles non extitistis, quod uerum est quis uobis credet? in nummo scilicet iniusto, non in creatore, quem et Marcion iustum facit, et: si in alieno fideles inuenti non estis, meum quis dabit uobis? alienum enim debet esse a semis dei quod iniustum est. creator autem quomodo alienus erat Pharisaeis, proprius deus Iudaicae gentis? si ergo haec non cadunt in creatorem, sed in mamonam, \'quis uobis credet quod uerius est\'? et \'quis uobis dabit quod meum est\'? non potest quasi ali{en)us dixisse de alterius dei gratia. tunc enim uideretur ita dixisse, si eos in creatorem, non in mamonam infideles notando per creatoris mentionem distinctione se fecisset dei alterius, non commissuri suam ueritatem infidelibus creatoris, t quoniam tunc alterius uideri potest, si non ad hoc proponatur, ut a re, de qua agitur, separetur. Si autem et iustificantes se coram hominibus Pharisaei spem mercedis in homine ponebant, illo eos sensu increpabat, quo et propheta Hieremias: miser homo, qui spem habet in homine. si et adicit: scit autem deus corda uestra, illius dei uim commemorabat, (qui) lucernam se pronuntiarat scrutantem renes et corda. si superbiam tangit: quod elatum est apud homines perosum est deo, Esaiam ponit ante oculos: dies enim domini Sabaoth in omnem contumeliosum et superbum, in omnem sublimem et elatum, et humiliabuntur. Possum iam colligere, cur tanto aeuo deus Marcionis fuerit in occulto. expectabat, opinor, donec haec omnia disceret a creatore. didicit igitur usque ad Iohannis tempora atque ita exinde processit adnuntiare regnum dei dicens: lex et prophetae usque ad Iohannem; ex quo regnum dei adnuntiatur. quasi non et nos limitem quendam agnoscamus Iohannem constitutum inter uetera et noua, ad quem desineret Iudaismus et a quo inciperet Christianismus, non tamen, ut ab alia uirtute facta sit sedatio legis et prophetarum et initiatio euangelii, in quo est dei regnum.\' [Christus ipse.] nam id si probauimus, et uetera transitura et noua successura praedicari a creatore, si et Iohannes antecursor et praeparator ostenditur uiarum domini euangelium\', superducturi et regnum dei promulgaturi, et ex hoc iam, quod Iohannes uenit, ipse erit Christus qui Iohannem erit subsecutus ut antecursorem; et, si desierunt uetera et coeperunt ! noua interstite Iohanne, non erit mirum quod ex dispositione est creatoris, ut unde(unde) magis probetur ** quam ex legis et prophetarum in Iohannem occasu et exinde ortu regni dei. transeat igitur caelum et terra citius, sicut et lex et: prophetae, quam unus apexuerborum domini-nerbum enim, inquit Esaias, dei nostri manet in aeuum —: nam quoniam in Esaia iam tunc Christus, sermo scilicet et spiritus creatoris, Iohannem praedicarat — uocem clamantis in deserto: parate uiam domini — in hoc uenturum, ut legis et] prophetarum ordo exinde cessaret, per adimpletionem, non per destructionem, et regnum dei a Christo adnuntiaretur, I ideo subtexuit facilius elementa transitura quam uerba sua,\' confirmans hoc quoque, quod de Iohanne dixerat, non praeterisse.
pass_a_gloss: To whom He says that two masters cannot be served, because it is necessary to offend one and defend the other, He Himself declares, proposing God and mammon. Therefore, mammon, which He wants to be understood, if you do not have an interpreter, you can learn from Him. For, warning us to look out for worldly friendships according to the example of that servant, who, having been removed from office, relieves his master's debtors by reducing their securities for his own benefit: and I, He says, tell you, make friends for yourselves from mammon of injustice, from money, of course, from which also that servant. For we know that money is the author and ruler of all worldly injustice. Seeing the greed of the Pharisees, He strengthened this statement: you cannot serve God and mammon. Finally, the Pharisees, who were greedy for money, ridiculed, because they understood, of course, that mammon was spoken of in terms of money, not because they thought that the creator should be understood in mammon and that Christ had recalled them from the service of the creator. What now? Rather, learn from this that Christ shows one God. For He named two masters, God and mammon, the creator and money: finally, you cannot serve God, certainly to Him, whom they seemed to serve, and mammon, to whom they were more devoted. But if He Himself were acting as another, He would have shown not two masters, but three — and the creator is indeed the Lord, because He is God, and certainly a greater Lord than mammon, and more to be obeyed by man, because He is a greater Lord —; what kind of thing is it, that He who said mammon was the master and joined it with the Lord, would be silent about the Lord Himself, that is, the creator God? Or did He, by being silent, concede that He should be served, if only He had denied that they could serve Him and mammon? Thus, when He sets forth one God, He names the creator, if He Himself were another, He named the creator, whom He set forth as Lord without another God. And this, therefore, will become clear, how it was said: if you have not been faithful in mammon of injustice, who will trust you? Certainly, in unjust money, not in the creator, whom Marcion also makes just, and: if you have not been faithful in what is another's, who will give you what is mine? For what is another's must be unjust, and separate from the semi-god. But how was the creator alien to the Pharisees, when He was the proper God of the Jewish people? If, therefore, these things do not fall upon the creator, but upon mammon, who will trust you, which is truer? And who will give you what is mine? He cannot have said this as if it were another's God's gift. For then He would have seemed to say this, if He had noted them as unfaithful in the creator, not in mammon, by mentioning the creator, making a distinction, and not entrusting His truth to the unfaithful creator. But if the Pharisees, justifying themselves before men, placed their hope of reward in men, He rebuked them with the same sense in which the prophet Jeremiah said: woe to the man who puts his hope in man. And if He adds: but God knows your hearts, He commemorated the power of that God, who declared Himself to be the searcher of kidneys and hearts. If He touches on pride: what is exalted among men is an abomination to God, He sets Isaiah before their eyes: for the day of the Lord of hosts will be upon every arrogant and haughty one, and they will be humbled. I can now gather why the God of Marcion was in hiding for so long. He was waiting, I think, until He had learned all these things from the creator. Therefore, He learned up to the time of John and thus proceeded to announce the kingdom of God, saying: the law and the prophets were until John; from whom the kingdom of God is announced. As if we also do not recognize a certain boundary established by John between the old and the new, at which Judaism ceased and Christianity began, not, however, that the cessation of the law and the prophets and the initiation of the gospel, in which is the kingdom of God, was made by another virtue. For if we have proven this, that the old things are passing away and the new things are succeeding, as predicted by the creator, and John is shown to be the forerunner and preparer of the ways of the Lord, and the gospel is to be brought and the kingdom of God is to be proclaimed, and from this, now that John has come, Christ Himself will be the one who follows John as a forerunner; and if the old things have ceased and the new things have begun, with John in between, it will not be surprising that this is from the disposition of the creator, so that it may be proven more than from the passing away of the law and the prophets in John and from the rising of the kingdom of God. Therefore, let heaven and earth pass away more quickly, just as the law and the prophets, than one dot of the Lord's words — for the word of our God remains forever —; for since in Isaiah, Christ, namely the speech and spirit of the creator, had already predicted John, saying: a voice crying in the desert: prepare the way of the Lord — in this, that the order of the law and the prophets would cease from then on, through fulfillment, not destruction, and the kingdom of God would be announced by Christ — therefore, He more easily affirmed that the elements would pass away than His own words, confirming also what He had said about John, that it had not passed away.

choices.why: The Latin word 'mamona' refers to wealth or riches, and in this context, it is used to describe the master that is opposed to God.
The Latin word 'deus' refers to God, and in this context, it is used to describe the master that is opposed to mammon.
The Latin word 'creator' refers to the creator of the world, and in this context, it is used to describe God.

bible_refs.note: You cannot serve God and mammon
If you have not been faithful in mammon of injustice, who will trust you?
A voice crying in the desert: prepare the way of the Lord

pass_b_english: He says two masters cannot be served, since one must inevitably be offended while the other is defended, and He makes this clear by naming them: God and mammon. So if you lack an interpreter for what He means by 'mammon,' you can learn it straight from Him. He warns us to secure our worldly friendships by the example of the steward who, once removed from office, slashed his master's debts to buy himself a safety net. 'And I tell you,' He says, 'make friends for yourselves with the mammon of injustice — that is, with money, the very stuff the steward used.' We all know money is the author and ruler of every injustice in the world. When He saw the Pharisees' greed slaving for it, He drove the point home: 'You cannot serve God and mammon' (Luke 16:13). The money-loving Pharisees sneered, because they understood perfectly that 'mammon' meant money — not that the Creator was meant by 'mammon' and that Christ had called them off from serving the Creator.

So learn this instead: Christ presents one God. He names two masters — God and mammon, the Creator and money — and says, 'You cannot serve God,' meaning the One they claimed to serve, 'and mammon,' the one they actually served. If Christ were a different God, He would have had to present three masters, not two: the Creator is Lord because He is God, and a far greater Lord than mammon, demanding far more obedience. What sense would it make for the One who called mammon a master and yoked it alongside the true Lord to then fall silent about the Lord Himself — that is, the Creator God? Or did His silence concede that the Creator should be served, just because He denied they could serve both Him and mammon? By setting forth one God, He names the Creator; if He were another, He would have named the Creator as Lord without any other God beside Him.

This clarifies the saying: 'If you have not been faithful in the mammon of injustice, who will trust you with what is true?' (Luke 16:11). That means unfaithful with unjust money, not with the Creator — whom Marcion even declares just. And: 'If you have not been faithful in what belongs to another, who will give you what is yours?' What belongs to another must be the unjust thing, alien to the Demiurge. But how was the Creator 'alien' to the Pharisees when He was the proper God of the Jewish nation? If these words do not strike the Creator but mammon, then 'who will trust you with what is truer?' and 'who will give you what is mine?' He could not have spoken as if the gift belonged to another's God. For that would only follow if He had charged them with unfaithfulness to the Creator rather than to mammon, distinguishing Himself by mentioning the Creator and withholding His truth from those unfaithful to the Creator — since only then would another God appear, separated from the matter at hand.

But if the Pharisees, justifying themselves before men, staked their hope of reward on men, He rebuked them in the same spirit as the prophet Jeremiah: 'Wretched is the man who puts his hope in man.' And when He adds, 'But God knows your hearts,' He invokes the power of that God who declared Himself the searcher of kidneys and hearts. When He strikes at pride — 'What is exalted among men is an abomination to God' — He sets Isaiah before their eyes: 'For the day of the Lord of hosts shall come upon every arrogant and haughty one, upon everyone lifted high, and they shall be humbled.'

I can now see why Marcion's God stayed hidden for so long. He was waiting, I suppose, until He had learned all this from the Creator. So He learned up to the time of John, and then emerged to announce the kingdom of God, saying: 'The Law and the Prophets were until John; from then on the kingdom of God is proclaimed.' As if we do not also recognize a boundary line drawn by John between the old and the new — where Judaism ends and Christianity begins — not, however, as if the Law and Prophets were silenced and the Gospel inaugurated by a different power. For if we have proven that the old passes away and the new succeeds, as predicted by the Creator; and if John is shown to be the forerunner and preparer of the Lord's ways; and if the Gospel is to be overlaid and the kingdom proclaimed — then from John's arrival onward, Christ Himself is the One who follows John as forerunner. And if the old ceased and the new began with John as the hinge, it is no surprise that this comes from the Creator's own design, so that it is proven more decisively by the passing of the Law and Prophets in John and the rising of the kingdom of God than by any other sign.

Therefore, let heaven and earth pass away sooner than one dot of the Lord's words — for 'the word of our God remains forever' — since in Isaiah, Christ, that is the Speech and Spirit of the Creator, had already foretold John: 'A voice crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord' (Isaiah 40:3) — in this, that the order of the Law and Prophets would cease from that point through fulfillment, not destruction, and the kingdom of God would be announced by Christ. That is why He more easily affirmed that the elements would pass away than His own words, confirming also what He had said about John: that it would not pass away.
